blocks.text: BULAKAN, Bulacan—Centuries-old arches that once symbolized the divide between the rich and the poor, even in death, remain standing at a Roman Catholic cemetery in this town, the former capital of Bulacan province. At the municipal cemetery behind the Nuestra Señora de la Asunción Church, at least two old arches still stand as reminders of the Spanish colonial practice of separating burial grounds according to a person’s economic and social status. Joey Meneses Rodrigo, a former municipal tourism and information officer, said the cemetery, much like Paco Park Cemetery in Manila, was divided into an inner section reserved for the principalia, […]...
